context.summary: Raised by T-inbox-v1 (GitHub #38), whose brief says to propose the mechanism and raise it before building it. Event files are named by their ULID under events/decision/<id>/, so the same event on two branches is the same path with the same bytes, which git merges without a conflict. Until this is answered, T-inbox-v1 shows branch decisions in the inbox as not answerable yet, and `decision answer` refuses them with a message naming this decision. Related: D-branch-decisions-visible (pending) asks whether to observe branches at all; this decision assumes T-inbox-v1's observe-branches view and asks only how an answer is recorded.

options.tradeoff: `decision answer` first copies the branch's DecisionRaised event file onto main byte for byte (same id, same path, original actor and time), then records DecisionDecided as today. When the PR merges, git sees the same file added on both sides and merges it cleanly. Main's log is always whole. Needs C-event-log text (a copied event is not a new write; its lane is checked against its own actor) and C-cli-json §3 text. The answer reaches the session when it restacks on main.

Show branch decisions but refuse to answer them until the PR merges. No contract change, but a session blocked on its own decision can't get an answer without merging unfinished work, which is the problem #38 describes.

Sessions must raise decisions on main (D-branch-decisions-visible's recommendation); branch decisions stay a read-only warning in the inbox. No contract change to the log, but one extra merge per decision, and sessions that forget are only caught by the warning.

data.question: T-inbox-v1 makes decisions raised on open PR branches visible in the lead's inbox ("raised on branch X, in PR #N"). An answer recorded on main would name a decision whose DecisionRaised event is only on the branch, so main's log would hold an answer to nothing until the PR merges, and could hold one forever if the PR is closed. How should `ekumen decision answer` work for such a decision?
data.title: How the lead answers a decision that is raised on an unmerged task branch
